## Layouts and rank maps (`distribute.layout`) {#sec-ch03-layouts}

A layout answers three questions for every block: where it sits in the block grid, which block is its neighbour in
each of the up to 26 directions, and which process owns it. Blocks are ranked in Morton (Z) order inside the block grid
or inside a panel, so that blocks close in space get close ranks; on the cubed sphere the ranks are face-major. Several
blocks may share one process; a block's rank then splits into a process rank and a local index. Periodicity is not a
layout key: it comes from the boundary names. How a decomposition is configured is also described with the
configuration keys in @sec-ch12-layout, and how the layout object is built with the block in @sec-ch01-layout.

Local symbols: $n_{\mathrm b,1}, n_{\mathrm b,2}, n_{\mathrm b,3}$ the number of blocks along
$x_1$, $x_2$, $x_3$ (YAML `nb1`, `nb2`, `nb3`; code `pz`, `px`, `py`; count); $(b_2, b_3, b_1)$ a block's index
along each axis in the block grid, as in @sec-ch03-globalgrid (code `(rx, ry, rz)`; count); $n_{\mathrm{bpp}}$ the
blocks per process (`blocks_per_process`; count).

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Cut the global grid into a block grid and number the blocks: `slab` (2-D in $x_2, x_3$), `cubed` (3-D,
the only one that splits $x_1$), `cubed-sphere` (six panels of $n_{\mathrm b,2}\times n_{\mathrm b,2}$); rank rule @eq-ch03-layouts-rank.

**Data.** In: YAML `distribute: {layout, nb1, nb2, nb3, blocks_per_process}` and the process count. Out: block
ranks, neighbours and periodic flags [-].

**Placement.** Setup.

**Activation.** `distribute.layout`; default `slab`, one block per axis, one block per process. `slab` and
`cubed-sphere` need $n_{\mathrm b,1} = 1$; `cubed-sphere` needs $n_{\mathrm b,2} = n_{\mathrm b,3}$.

**Guarantee / limits.** N/A for accuracy; every block gets one global rank (face-major Morton order on the cubed sphere).

**Evidence.** `test_exchange_decomp` (up to six processes), `test_mesh_exchange_python`; check `[C10]`; the ctest
entries were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

### Derivation

The rank maps are definitions, not approximations; the derivation states them. Within a block grid of $n_{\mathrm b,2}\times n_{\mathrm b,3}$
(or $n_{\mathrm b,2}\times n_{\mathrm b,3}\times n_{\mathrm b,1}$) blocks, rank $\mathrm{rank}$ is the $\mathrm{rank}$-th valid point of the Morton curve: the codes
$0, 1, 2, \dots$ are decoded with $b_2$ the even bits and $b_3$ the odd bits (three interleaved bit sets in 3-D), codes
that fall outside the block grid are skipped, and the $\mathrm{rank}$-th surviving code is the location of that rank,
in `build_zorder_coords2` ({{< code src/layout/connectivity.cpp build_zorder_coords2 >}}), with the decoder `morton_decode2`
({{< code src/layout/connectivity.hpp morton_decode2 >}}). On the cubed sphere the global rank of the block at Morton rank $\mathrm{rank}_f$
on face $f$ is face-major, and with $n_{\mathrm{bpp}}$ blocks per process a block's rank splits as

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{rank} &= f\,n_{\mathrm b,2}^2 + \mathrm{rank}_f, \\
\mathrm{rank} &= n_{\mathrm{bpp}}\,\mathrm{proc} + \mathrm{loc}, \qquad 0 \le \mathrm{loc} < n_{\mathrm{bpp}},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-layouts-rank}

with $f = 0..5$ the panel, $\mathrm{rank}_f$ the block's rank inside panel $f$, $\mathrm{proc}$ the owning process and
$\mathrm{loc}$ the local index on that process (upright names, so that none reads as a density, a constant or a
wavelength). The first row is
`_global_rank_from_face_local` ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.hpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl >}}), the second `owner_process_rank`,
`local_block_index` and `global_block_rank` ({{< code src/layout/layout.hpp LayoutOptionsImpl >}}).

A neighbour inside the block grid is the location plus the offset, wrapped when the axis is periodic and absent
($-1$) otherwise. On the cubed sphere a step across a panel edge goes through the edge table `CS_FACE_EDGES`: leaving
face $f$ across one of its four edges arrives on face $f'$ across the edge the table pairs with it, with the along-edge block index reversed when the table says
so ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CS_FACE_EDGES >}}). A corner step is two edge steps, ordered so that the first stays
on the panel when it can in `neighbor_rank` ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::neighbor_rank >}}). Every map here is exact.

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
The Morton order of a $4\times4$ block grid is checked exactly (`[C10]`).[^lay-c10]
:::

[^lay-c10]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C10]`; a numpy port of `build_zorder_coords2` and its decoder at the pin, CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

The layout is set up once, when the block is built, and is not part of a stage. The YAML maps `nb2` to $n_{\mathrm b,2}$ (the
$x_2$ direction), `nb3` to $n_{\mathrm b,3}$ ($x_3$) and `nb1` to $n_{\mathrm b,1}$ ($x_1$); `repartition` then gives each block its share of
the global grid (@sec-ch03-globalgrid). The number of blocks the processes hold together must equal $n_{\mathrm b,1}n_{\mathrm b,2}n_{\mathrm b,3}$, six
times that on the cubed sphere, or setup stops. Periodic flags are set from the boundary names: `periodic` on $x_2$ or
$x_3$ sets the flag on every layout, `periodic` on $x_1$ only on `cubed`. @fig-ch03-layouts-morton draws the Morton
order of a $4\times4$ block grid and the face numbering of the cube.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-layouts-morton
#| fig-cap: "(a) Rank order of a $4\\times4$ block grid: Morton (Z) order, with $b_2$ along $x_2$ and $b_3$ along $x_3$; the line joins consecutive ranks. (b) The cubed-sphere face numbering $0$ to $5$ ($+X$, $+Y$, $-X$, $+Z$, $-Y$, $-Z$) as an unfolded net."
#| fig-alt: "Left, a four by four grid of numbered squares joined by a Z-shaped curve; right, the cross-shaped net of the cube with face numbers and small axis arrows."
#| echo: false
```

: Code map of the layouts. {#tbl-ch03-layouts-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-layouts-code):

1. `from_yaml` reads `layout` (default `slab`), `nb3` into `py`, `nb2` into `px`, `nb1` into `pz`; `backend` is an
   accepted but dead key, read from the `BACKEND` environment variable instead ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. The mesh options read the number of blocks per process, default 1, in `from_yaml`
   ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). The mesh then sets the world size to
   processes times blocks in `reset` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::reset >}}).
3. `slab` refuses a `pz` other than 1 with "pz must be 1 for slab layout" ({{< code src/layout/slab_layout.cpp SlabLayoutImpl::_initialize >}});
   `cubed-sphere` refuses a `pz` other than 1 and `px` unequal to `py` ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::_initialize >}});
   for any other layout name `create` stops with "Unsupported layout type" ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::create >}}).
4. The boundary names set `periodic_x`, `periodic_y` and, on `cubed`, `periodic_z`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
5. Each exchange asks `neighbor_rank` for the peer of each direction
   ({{< code src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp CubedSphereLayoutImpl::neighbor_rank >}}).

**How to use it.** The block grid and the blocks per process are the `distribute` block; periodicity comes from the
boundary names (@sec-ch03-physfaces). An $x_1$ split needs `cubed`:

```yaml
distribute:
  layout: cubed          # slab (default) or cubed-sphere; only cubed accepts nb1 > 1
  nb1: 2                 # blocks along x1; nb2, nb3 along x2, x3 (default 1)
  blocks_per_process: 2  # blocks held by one process (default 1); processes x blocks must equal nb1 nb2 nb3
```

Refused, each with its message:

- a key outside `layout`, `nb1`–`nb3`, `verbose`, `blocks_per_process` and `backend`: "unknown key 'distribute/nb4'.
  Valid keys: …";
- an unknown layout: "Unsupported layout type: slabs";
- `nb1` > 1 on `slab`: "SlabLayoutImpl: pz must be 1 for slab layout", and on `cubed-sphere` its own two messages
  (@sec-ch03-gnomonic);
- a block count that the processes do not hold: "MeshBlockImpl: world_size (1) does not match layout partitioning
  (2)."

`backend` is accepted and ignored. The reading of the keys and the type dispatch are
({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}, {{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::create >}}):

```cpp
  check_keys(node, "distribute",
             {"layout", "nb1", "nb2", "nb3", "verbose", "blocks_per_process",
              "backend"});  // dead since #181; BACKEND env

  op->type() = node["layout"].as<std::string>("slab");
  op->py(node["nb3"].as<int>(1));
  op->px(node["nb2"].as<int>(1));
  op->pz(node["nb1"].as<int>(1));
  op->backend() = get_env("BACKEND", op->backend());
    ...
  if (options->type() == "slab") {
    pl = std::make_shared<SlabLayoutImpl>(options, p);
  } else if (options->type() == "cubed") {
    pl = std::make_shared<CubedLayoutImpl>(options, p);
  } else if (options->type() == "cubed-sphere") {
    pl = std::make_shared<CubedSphereLayoutImpl>(options, p);
  } else {
    TORCH_CHECK(false, "Unsupported layout type: ", options->type());
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_exchange_decomp` | ghosts hold the expected neighbour, with local and remote neighbours both seen, for 1 process × 6 blocks, 6 × 1 and 2 × 3 | value bounds per ghost | payloads chosen to identify the sender |
| `test_mesh_exchange_python` | on a $2\times2$ slab in one process each ghost equals its neighbour's rank | exact | integer payloads |

: Tests of the layouts. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-layouts-tests}

`test_exchange_decomp` runs `test_exchange` under `torchrun` on gloo in the three cases of `cases`
({{< code tests/run_exchange_decomp.py main >}}); the comparison is `ghosts_match_expected`
({{< code tests/test_exchange.cpp ghosts_match_expected >}}) on the cubed-sphere deck `test_exchange.yaml`. The slab case,
`test_mesh_exchange.py`, sets four blocks with `set_local_horizontal_cells` in a top-level script
({{< code tests/test_mesh_exchange.py >}}). Both run on CPU;
`test_exchange_decomp` uses up to six processes and runs alone. They were not run for this chapter at the pin
(missing evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Only `cubed` splits $x_1$; the cubed sphere forces $n_{\mathrm b,1} = 1$.
- `distribute.backend` is accepted and ignored; the backend comes from `BACKEND`.
:::

The Morton order of `cubed` in 3-D and the corner steps of the cubed sphere with $n_{\mathrm b,2} > 1$ have no dedicated test
(read from the tests; not measured). The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
